sentences.text:
1  D1-II FLOOR, AMRITHA TOWERS KPXX JUNCTION OPPOSITE  MAHARAJA GROUNDS, M.G. ROAD ERNAKULAM REPRESENTED BY  ITS DIVISIONAL MANAGER, PIN - 682011  BY ADVS.
 SRI.VPK.PANICKER  SHRI.P.JACOB MATHEW  SRI.MATHEWS JACOB (SR.)
 THIS MFA (ECC) HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 08.09.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:66576 MFA (ECC) NO. 79 OF 2024  3  JUDGMENT 1. Appellant is the Applicant before the Employees Compensation Commissioner.

The Commissioner allowed the Application filed by the applicant, granting a compensation of Rs.9,98,304/-, with interest at the rate of 12% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment, Rs.3,66,873/- towards reimbursement of medical expenditure and Rs.2,000/- towards the payment of Court Fee.

The Commissioner has found that there is 100% functional disability to the applicant and calculated the compensation on the basis of a monthly wage at the rate of Rs.8,000/-
per month.

2. This Court admitted this appeal on the following substantial questions of law:
i.

Whether the Commissioner erred in reckoning an amount of Rs.8,000/- as monthly wages as against the 2025:KER:66576 MFA (ECC) NO. 79 OF 2024 amount of Rs.9,600/-, the amount prescribed as minimum wage of a car driver in an accident which occurred on 14.07.2012?
ii. Whether the Commissioner erred in rejecting the order of 12% interest to Rs.3,66,873/- ordered as reimbursement of medical expenditure from the date of accident till the date of payment?
3. I heard the learned counsel for the appellant, Smt. Farah Jyothi Pradeep and the learned counsel for the 2nd respondent, Sri. V.P.K. Panicker.

4. The learned counsel for the appellant contended that the monthly wages of Rs.8,000/- fixed by the Commissioner is liable to be increased in view of the judgment of this Court dated 25.06.2025 in Sooraj vs Binoy C.P on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119969116/
2 M.F.A. (ECC) No.62/2018.

In the said judgment, this Court following the decision of the Madras High Court in Saraswathi and Others v. Pacifica Chennai Project Infrastructure Co. Pvt. Ltd.
2025:KER:66576 MFA (ECC) NO. 79 OF 2024 and Others [2020 ACJ 79] held that the monthly wages was fixed by the Central Government as per Notification dated 31.05.2010 under Section 4(1B) of the Employee's Compensation Act and thereafter it was revised only after 10 years; that as per Section 4(1B) of the Employee's Compensation Act, the monthly wages has to be notified by the Central Government from time to time; and that the employees should not be prejudiced on account of the default on the part of the Central Government in issuing Notifications fixing the monthly wages taking into account the increase of the wages from time to time.

entities.text:
Saraswathi and Others v. Pacifica Chennai Project Infrastructure Co. Pvt. Ltd.
2025:KER:66576 MFA (ECC) NO. 79 OF 2024 and Others [2020 ACJ 79]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the fact that Rs.8000/- fixed as per the Notification dated 31.05.2010 was revised to Rs.15000/- as per Notification dated 03.01.2020 thereby increasing Rs.7000/- for 10 years, increase at the rate of Rs.700/- per year was added for the period of two years after the Notification dated 31.05.2010 in the said case to Rs.8000/- and thus fixed the monthly wages at Rs.9,400/-.
The Applicant in the 2025:KER:66576 MFA (ECC) NO. 79 OF 2024 said case was also a driver by profession.

Even though the applicant therein claimed calculation based on monthly wages of Rs.15,600/- in accordance with the Kerala Fair Wages Act on the basis of the Supreme Court decision in Manusha Sreekumar and Others v. United India Insurance Company Ltd. [(2022) 17 SCC 321], this Court rejected the prayer, holding that the said decision was one rendered under the Motor Vehicles Act,
where there is no wage ceiling.

entities.text: Manusha Sreekumar and Others v. United India Insurance Company Ltd. [(2022) 17 SCC 321]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In this case also, the accident happened roughly two years after the Notification dated 31.05.2010, and hence, in view of the aforesaid judgment in M.F.A. (ECC)
No.62/2018, the Applicant is entitled to get fixation of monthly wages at Rs.9,400/- for calculating the compensation.
In such a case, the compensation will be Rs.11,73,007/- (9,400 x 60/100 x 100/100 x 207.98).

The additional compensation would be Rs.1,74,703/- (Rs.11,73,007/- -
Rs.9,98,304/-).
The substantial question of law No.1 is thus answered in favour of the appellant.
The next contention is that the Applicant is entitled to get interest for the reimbursement of medical expenditure.

The learned counsel for the Appellant cited the decision of this Court in Venugopalan v. The Managing Partner, Cheeni Packaging, Paduvapuram and Another [2023 KHC 672] in which this Court considered the very same question and found that the claimant is entitled to get interest at the rate of 12% on medical reimbursement from the date of the petition till realization.

entities.text: Venugopalan v. The Managing Partner, Cheeni Packaging, Paduvapuram and Another [2023 KHC 672]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the Applicant in this case is also entitled to get interest at the rate of 12%
per annum from the date of the petition till realization on the amount of Rs.3,66,873/- awarded towards reimbursement of medical expenditure.
The substantial question of law No.2 is thus answered in favour of the appellant.

6. The learned counsel for the 2nd respondent pointed out that the 2nd respondent has already deposited the award amount of Rs.9,98,304/- with interest at the rate of 12% as ordered in the 2025:KER:66576 MFA (ECC) NO. 79 OF 2024 impugned award and also the medical expenditure of Rs.3,66,873/-.

If the amount deposited towards compensation is adjusted against Rs.11,73,007/-
and interest thereon, it would be an undue enrichment to the Applicant.

Hence, the direction in this appeal may be limited to pay the additional compensation and interest thereon and also to pay the Sooraj vs Binoy C.P on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119969116/
3 interest alone with respect to the medical expenditure.
I find force in the said contention and the same is accepted.

7. The learned counsel for the 2nd respondent also pointed out that there was a delay of 382 days in filing this appeal and the same was condoned and the 2nd respondent may not be held liable to pay interest for the said period of delay that happened due to the fault of the Appellant.
The said contention is found reasonable and accepted.

8. Accordingly, this appeal is allowed without costs, granting an additional compensation of Rs.1,74,703/- with interest @ 12% per 2025:KER:66576 MFA (ECC) NO. 79 OF 2024 annum from the date of accident, i.e., 14.07.2012 till the date of payment and interest @ 12% per annum from the date of petition till deposit of Rs.3,66,873/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Commissioner.
The period of delay of 382 days shall be excluded while calculating interest on the additional compensation of Rs.1,74,703/-.

Sd/-
